prompt: Each case illustrates a characteristic of B2B market structure or demand behavior. Identify which concept applies.

options.label: Pulling derived demand via end consumers

cases.text: A jet engine manufacturer sells to only a handful of commercial aircraft builders clustered around Seattle and Toulouse, with each contract worth hundreds of millions of dollars.
cases.explanation: B2B marketers typically deal with far fewer and much larger buyers than consumer marketers do, often concentrated in industrial clusters.

cases.text: Orders for automotive leather upholstery fall by fifteen percent after higher interest rates reduce household purchases of new SUVs at dealerships.
cases.explanation: Business demand for upholstery is derived demand because it ultimately comes from downstream consumer demand for vehicles.

cases.text: A chemical firm advertises its breathable waterproof membrane directly to hikers on television so shoppers look for its hangtag when buying outdoor jackets.
cases.explanation: Because derived demand originates with end consumers, B2B suppliers sometimes advertise directly to final consumers to pull demand through the supply chain.

cases.text: When residential home buying slows down, a structural timber mill and an insulation manufacturer both see immediate drops in orders from builders.
cases.explanation: Commercial demand for construction materials derives directly from household demand for finished homes.

cases.text: A maker of extreme-ultraviolet lithography systems serves five semiconductor foundries worldwide rather than millions of individual shoppers.
cases.explanation: A small number of very large organizational buyers accounts for the entire market volume.

prompt: Identify which business buying concept best describes each organizational purchase.

cases.text: A distribution warehouse routinely reorders the same stretch wrap and shipping labels from an approved vendor list without changing any terms.
cases.explanation: In a straight rebuy, the buyer routinely reorders an item without any modifications.

cases.text: A coffee chain asks its existing packaging vendor to switch to compostable fiber lids and revise the unit price and delivery schedule.
cases.explanation: In a modified rebuy, the buyer modifies product specifications, prices, delivery terms, or suppliers.

cases.text: A regional bakery purchases its first automated robotic bread-slicing line and forms a cross-departmental team to research vendors from scratch.
cases.explanation: In a new-task situation, a company buys a product or service for the first time, requiring more participants and extensive search.

cases.text: Rather than buying servers, cooling units, power backups, and monitoring software separately, a bank contracts one prime vendor to deliver a complete turnkey data center.
cases.explanation: Systems selling (solutions selling) provides a complete turnkey package of interlocked products and services from a single prime contractor.

cases.text: A competing industrial adhesive maker pitches a faster-curing formula to a furniture factory that is reviewing its annual supply agreement.
cases.explanation: A modified rebuy gives out suppliers an opening to pitch a better offer while in suppliers work to protect the account.

prompt: A commercial airline is purchasing new cabin seating. Identify which buying center role each participant plays.

cases.text: Flight attendants and cabin maintenance crews report that current seat latches jam during turnaround cleaning and request a durable replacement.
cases.explanation: Users are the members of the organization who actually use the product, often initiating the proposal and helping define functional needs.

cases.text: An aerospace materials engineer specifies the flame-retardant foam density and maximum weight limits that candidate seats must meet.
cases.explanation: Influencers affect the buying decision by helping define technical specifications and providing criteria for evaluating alternatives.

cases.text: The vice president of procurement negotiates volume discounts, warranty terms, and delivery penalties with the seat manufacturer.
cases.explanation: Buyers hold formal organizational authority to select the supplier and arrange terms of purchase.

cases.text: An external ergonomics consultant submits test data comparing lumbar support and passenger legroom across three seat designs.
cases.explanation: External specialists who supply evaluation data and technical recommendations act as influencers.

cases.text: A senior contracting officer drafts the purchase agreement and payment schedule once the supplier specifications are set.
cases.explanation: Arranging purchase terms and executing the procurement contract is the responsibility of the buyer.

prompt: Match each early stage or method in the business buying decision process with the factory action that illustrates it.

pairs.match: A packaging line supervisor notices that a sealing machine is jamming twice per hour and slowing daily shipments.
pairs.explanation: Problem recognition occurs when someone in the company recognizes a problem or need triggered internally or externally.

pairs.match: The plant manager writes a summary stating that the facility needs two high-speed thermal sealers capable of running 120 cartons per minute.
pairs.explanation: General need description summarizes the general characteristics, reliability, and output capacity of the needed item.

pairs.match: Mechanical engineers draft detailed blueprint tolerances, voltage requirements, and stainless-steel grade standards for the new sealers.
pairs.explanation: Product specification defines the exact technical characteristics required for the item.

pairs.match: The engineering team studies whether a custom milled bracket on the sealer can be replaced with a standard stamped part at forty percent lower cost.
pairs.explanation: Value analysis examines components to determine whether they can be redesigned, standardized, or made by less costly methods.

question_text: An industrial robotics manufacturer discovers that 18 percent of its corporate clients generate 82 percent of its annual revenue. Rather than sending standard product catalogs, the firm assigns dedicated teams of engineers, logistics planners, and account directors to co-design assembly cells and coordinate service across each client's global plants. What strategy is the manufacturer executing?
hint: Consider how B2B firms structure cross-functional teams around the Pareto concentration of their highest-value accounts.

options.option_text: Transactional marketing aimed at maximizing immediate surplus on each isolated equipment order.
options.option_explanation: Transactional marketing treats each order as a one-off negotiation rather than embedding cross-functional teams for long-term co-design.

options.option_text: A straight rebuy automation program for routine maintenance supplies.
options.option_explanation: Straight rebuys involve routine reordering of standard items without modifications, not custom engineering partnerships.

options.option_text: Key Account Management (KAM) focused on deep, long-term partnerships with its most valuable organizational customers.
options.option_explanation: Correct. KAM assigns dedicated cross-functional teams to co-design customized solutions, align supply schedules, and coordinate global service for top accounts.

options.option_text: Government open-tender bidding under public regulatory compliance.
options.option_explanation: The scenario describes dedicated cross-functional account teams serving commercial manufacturers, not public-sector open tenders.

prompt: Match each buying center role in an AI-enabled enterprise with the participant and action that perform it.

pairs.match: An automated procurement agent detects that safety gloves are below reorder threshold and issues a purchase order under pre-approved contract terms.
pairs.explanation: In a straight rebuy, an automated procurement agent monitors stock and reorders standard supplies within contract rules, acting directly as the buyer.

pairs.match: An AI sourcing agent parses 400 vendor catalogs and forwards only the three suppliers with valid ISO certifications to the human procurement team.
pairs.explanation: By filtering hundreds of catalogs and passing only a compliant shortlist to human officers, the AI agent acts as a gatekeeper.

pairs.match: An AI agent compares technical specification sheets, calculates five-year total cost of ownership across bids, and scores vendor delivery reliability.
pairs.explanation: When an AI agent analyzes specifications, lifecycle costs, and reliability metrics to shape evaluation, it acts as an influencer.

pairs.term: Decider in a high-risk new task
pairs.match: A committee of senior hospital executives signs off on the final vendor for a multi-million-dollar surgical robotics platform.
pairs.explanation: In high-risk modified rebuys and new-task purchases, human executives remain the final deciders because strategic, legal, and operational accountability rests with people.

prompt: Sort each B2B marketing action by whether it is designed to pass automated AI agent screening or to win over human decision makers after making the shortlist.

cards.text: Publishing structured, machine-readable technical tolerances and compatibility tables instead of unindexed PDF brochures.
cards.explanation: AI sourcing agents require machine-readable technical specifications and skip unindexed catalogs under lookup constraints.

cards.text: Exposing transparent volume pricing tiers, verified ISO and SOC 2 compliance certificates, and historical on-time delivery metrics.
cards.explanation: Automated gatekeepers filter vendors by transparent volume pricing, verified compliance certifications, and delivery records.

cards.text: Negotiating custom warranty terms and phased payment milestones with the client's chief financial officer.
cards.explanation: Once on the shortlist, human account managers negotiate custom contract terms with human executives.

cards.text: Building interpersonal trust with plant managers and guiding their teams through complex operational change during installation.
cards.explanation: Human salespeople and key account managers remain indispensable for interpersonal trust and organizational change management.
